original_question: For the unrestricted partition generating function product over m >= 1 of (1 + x^m + x^(2m) + ...), can one choose signs in some of the factors so that, after expansion, every coefficient belongs to {0, -1, 1}?
target_in_paper: Section 2014.2, item 2014.2.2 ('David Newman. About partitions'), where the notes ask whether one can change some of the plus signs in the right-hand-side expansion of the unrestricted partition generating function so that every coefficient of the expanded series is in {-1,0,1}. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the unrestricted partition generating function prod_{m>=1} 1/(1-x^m) = prod_{m>=1}(1 + x^m + x^{2m} + ...), and it also captures the paper's central coefficient constraint: after the sign changes and expansion, every coefficient should lie in {-1,0,1}. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
missing_details: The paper phrases the operation as changing some of the plus signs on the right-hand side to minus signs; the draft's wording 'choose signs in some of the factors' is ambiguous and could be read as changing whole factors rather than individual signs in the displayed product. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

Because the product is infinite, the natural ambient object is the formal power series ring Z[[x]]; 'after expansion' should be understood coefficientwise in that ring. This is implicit in the paper's generating-function notation but not stated in the draft. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The existence quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether there exists a global sign assignment for all relevant terms, not merely one that works up to a finite cutoff. The paper separately notes only a finite example through x^101. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

The constant term in each geometric-series factor remains 1; the sign choices concern the nonconstant terms appearing on the right-hand side of prod_{m>=1}(1 + x^m + x^{2m} + ...). ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))

To make the question mathematically stand-alone, one should write an explicit sign-parametrized product such as prod_{m>=1}(1 + epsilon_{m,1} x^m + epsilon_{m,2} x^{2m} + ...), with epsilon_{m,k} in {-1,1}. This formalizes the paper's wording without broadening it. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
refined_question: In the formal power series ring Z[[x]], does there exist a choice of signs epsilon_{m,k} in {-1,1} for every m >= 1 and k >= 1 such that, after replacing the right-hand side of prod_{m>=1} 1/(1-x^m) = prod_{m>=1}(1 + x^m + x^{2m} + ...) by prod_{m>=1}(1 + epsilon_{m,1} x^m + epsilon_{m,2} x^{2m} + ...), every coefficient of the resulting expanded series belongs to {-1,0,1}? ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Newman's partition question in Section 2014.2.2. The surrounding context first recalls the distinct-parts product prod_n (1+x^n), then the signed product prod_n (1-x^n) = 1 - x - x^2 + x^5 + x^7 + ..., and then immediately rewrites the unrestricted partition generating function as prod_n 1/(1-x^n) = (1+x+x^2+...)(1+x^2+x^4+...)... before asking whether changing some of the plus signs on that right-hand side can make all coefficients lie in {-1,0,1}. That is the nearest official formulation in the paper, and it is narrower and more faithful than phrasing the problem as a broader question about arbitrary modified partition products. The paper's note that Newman had an example working up to x^101 further indicates that the intended problem is a global existence question, not merely a finite-truncation one. ([theoryofnumbers.com](https://www.theoryofnumbers.com/cant/CANTProblemSessions.pdf))
